parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This unit fails because its two files handle persistence in different ways. SchedulingService.ts saves and loads data only through the module's DAO ports: it injects PatientDao and AppointmentDao and turns the rows they return into business entities (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment). VisitNotesService.ts skips that DAO layer. It injects PrismaService, which is an ORM client, and calls prisma.visitNote.create and prisma.visitNote.findMany directly. It also maps the raw rows into an ad-hoc VisitNote interface instead of a business entity.

The rubric fails a file that uses an ORM directly where the module reaches persistence through a repository or port, or that bypasses the module's own abstractions. The source confirms both candidate flags (lines 13-15 and line 20). I can't see whether a VisitNoteDao exists, so whether a repository is being bypassed for this exact table is less certain. Even so, the module plainly uses DAOs for persistence and VisitNotesService doesn't follow that pattern.

The concerns themselves fit together, since visit notes belong to appointments. In SchedulingService, the row-to-Appointment mapping is written out twice (in book and in cancel). That is repeated mapping code rather than a duplicated business rule, so it is only a minor issue.

violations.message: VisitNotesService calls the Prisma ORM directly (prisma.visitNote.create, prisma.visitNote.findMany) through an injected PrismaService. This bypasses the DAO/port abstraction the module uses for persistence (PatientDao, AppointmentDao in SchedulingService). It also returns an ad-hoc VisitNote interface instead of a business entity, so the module's abstractions aren't used consistently.
